newsitem.title: UK: Caspian says new CIS debt fund to be launched.
newsitem.headline: Caspian says new CIS debt fund to be launched.

text.p: Caspian Securities said on Friday it was lead managing the launch of a new Cayman Islands-registered fund investing in high-yielding Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) debt.

It said the Cossack Bond Company would invest in sovereign and regional debt issued by the Russian Federation, autonomous Russian republics and members of the CIS, particularly Ukraine, Moldova, Armenia, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan.
"The aim is to achieve yields considerably in excess of those provided by Russian U.S. dollar denominated debt, currently yielding approximately 10 percent," Caspian said in a statement.
The investment manager for the open-ended fund is emerging markets specialist Global Fund Management S.A.
The fund will be listed in Bermuda.
A Caspian spokesman said the fund would be capped at $50 million. It will be closed initially for six months following a May 30 closing. The launch date is May 28.
He said it was being marketed in the UK, Europe, Middle and Far East.

The fund will look to invest in the sovereign debt of countries moving to a stage of macro-economic stabilisation, while it will also look at regional, municipal and corporate debt of countries that have reached sustainable growth.
It said areas in the stabilisation stage, with tight monetary policy and a stable exchange rate policy, offered high yields in dollar terms.
"Investment in debt of stabilising countries produces equity level returns at substantially lower risk," it said.
